newsitem.title: AFRICA: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

GHANA, July 21 - Tema - Oil berth vacant. There was an explosion at the oil refinery killing 2 men. The cause is not yet known. Two tankers are waiting at anchorage. Refinery is unable to advise on berthing prospects. No other tankers are currently due at the port.

ISRAEL, July 22 - Haifa - Five vessels due, 1-2 days delay expected. Vessels discharging at berth, 5 general cargo, 1 bulk. Loading/discharging at berth, 4 containers, 3 tankers, 1 bulk waiting at anchorage to discharge. 2 Vessels waiting at anchorage to load/discharge of which 1 container vessel, 1 tanker. 2 Vessels under repair. Ashdod - Two to three days delay expected. Discharging at berth, 4 general cargo, 1 bulk, 3 containers loading/discharging at berth, 1 general cargo and 1 bulk waiting at anchorage to discharge, 1 bulk waiting at anchorage to load. 1 Tanker waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, 2 vessels awaiting orders. Eilat - No vessels.
JORDAN, July 19 - Aqaba - Four vessels loading at berth, 6 discharging at berth, 4 waiting at anchorage to load, 2 waiting at anchorage to discharge, 2 awaiting orders.

MOZAMBIQUE, July 21 - Nacala - Port working normally (first come, first served basis). No restriction on berthing and sailing at night. Draft restriction 9.5 metres at general cargo berths, 14 metres at container berths. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths working normally. 24 hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 140 metres loa. Some restriction for larger vessels and subject to arrangements with port captain. Max. draft for 24 hour navigation 7.5 metres. 2 Tugs available. General access channel - 2 Waverider buoys deployed in approach channel. Approx. diameter 1 metre with flashing orange light, flash frequency five one second flashes every 26 seconds. Maputo - Berthing/sailing of 24 hours for vessels up to 120 metres loa. Some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to arrangement with port captain. All berths fluid. Draft restriction in channel 9 metres less 0.5 metres plus rise of tide of the day. Max. draft for 24 hour navigation 9 metres.
NAMIBIA, July 21 - Walvis Bay - Working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, July 21 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths - Working normally. Bulk import berths - Delays 3-5 days. Bulk export berths (minerals etc) - Congested, delays approx 48 hours. Bulk coal berths - 2 Vessels alongside, 2 anchored, 16 due by 28/7. Berthing delays, 12-24 hours currently. Durban - Container terminal delays up to 60 hours expected whilst new crane being positioned at container terminal. Point/New Pier/Maydon Wharf berths - Fld for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal - 1 Vessel due in July, 5 due in August. Bunker suppliers - Fluid, but this could change daily due to bunching of vessels. East London - General cargo/combi terminal/tanker berths - Extremely busy, but no delays expected at this stage. Drydock - Fully booked until mid-December. Two tankers due weekly. Port Elizabeth - Port working normally. 1 Vessel in port, no delays expected for general, fruit or tanker berths. Fruit berth vacant. Container berth - 2 Gantry cranes available for 24 hours, 1 crane for 12 hours on day

Cape Town - Breakbulk berths - General cargo numerous bulk dischargers are expected until the end of the month, and possible delays may occur. Fruit berth - Easing off due to non-availability of fruit. Container terminal - Working normally, with vessels berthing and working on arrival. Bunker berths - Vessels berthing and bunkering on arrival. Drydocks and repair quay - Currently fully occupied and booking essential. Saldanha Bay - Working normally.

TUNISIA, July 19 - Tunis - Five vessels in port of which 3 awaiting instructions, 1 general cargo, 1 motor tanker loading oil. Rades - Five vessels in port of which 1 military, 3 ro-ro, 1 discharging containers. Goulette - North side - 5 Vessels of which 2 cereal, 1 discharging cars, 1 general cargo. South side - 3 Vessels of which 1 discharging grain, 1 motor tanker, 1 loading clinker. 3 Vessels in roads. Sfax - Six vessels operating of which 1 loading bulk tsp, 1 loading bulk sulphate, 1 loading bulk rock phosphate, 1 loading bulk salt, 2 discharging timber. Sousse - One vessel in port discharging woodpulp. No waiting time.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, July 19 - Dubai - Containers, 28 vessels due. No delays expected. 3 Loading at berth, 1 under repair/laid up. General cargo, 12 vessels due, no delays expected. 6 Vessels discharging at berth, 1 bunkering, 2 under repair/laid up. Tankers, 5 vessels due. No delays expected. 2 Vessels discharging at berth, 9 under repair/laid up.

YEMEN, July 20 - Hodeidah - Berths 1 and 5 are occupied. All other berths are vacant. 2 Vessels alongside of which 1 timber, 1 general cargo. 4 Vessels anchored carrying wheat flour. Berthing delays, general cargo up to 1 day, bagged cargo up to 3 days, bulk cargo up to 5 days, containers up to 1 day. Mokha - No vessels in port.
